confirmedCause: The pinned ag-http2:connection-close always invokes usocket:socket-shutdown, including after an earlier close. On SBCL closing the usocket FD stream leaves the underlying socket object descriptor intact. A second shutdown can target an unrelated new connection that reuses that descriptor.

upstreamNegativeControl.method: Restore the true upstream finalizer in-process and run exact FD-reuse, overlap and cleanup-error regressions.

socketOnlyFallbackNegativeControl.method: Force an actual thread interrupt after ownership claim, before upstream entry; real gRPC message buffer and flow-control waiters are active.
socketOnlyFallbackNegativeControl.finding: Socket closure and flow-CV notification alone leave the gRPC message reader stranded because its pending stream callback was never invoked.

stressFailurePreserved.interpretation: The independently proven close bugs are corrected; a separate intermittent startup/transport symptom remains under podster-uqb.18. No retries or deadlines were increased.

cleanupGuarantees: One atomic weak-key claim owns each connection finalization for the lifetime of that object, including upstream errors.
ASDF reloads preserve the true upstream function and do not stack wrappers.
On interrupted ownership handoff, pending unclaimed stream callbacks run through upstream at-most-once cleanup before unwind-protected socket release.
Message-buffer and flow-control waiters are exercised directly; callbacks already invoked are not replayed.
Closed socket streams are never shut down again; actual reused descriptors remain usable in the regressions.
